newsitem.title: USA: Three utilities join voluntary US climate program.
newsitem.headline: Three utilities join voluntary US climate program.

text.p: Three electric utility companies have joined a voluntary U.S. Energy Department program to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the department said Wednesday.

The companies were PECO Energy Co, which committed to a total reduction of 5 million short tons of carbon dioxide emissions in 2000, Tucson Electric Power Co, which committed to a 423,000 short ton reduction in 2000, and Hawaiian Electric Company which committed to a 632,000 short ton reduction.

The companies said they would use "a diverse portfolio of greenhouse gas reductions projects that also satisfy the electricity needs of their customers and help clean the environment," the Energy Department said.
PECO is to upgrade efficiency of existing nuclear and hydro units, as well as switching to lower carbon natural gas, coal combustion byproduct recycling and other measures.
Tucson Electric will do carbon-reducing power projects in Honduras and the Czech Republic as well as domestic initiatives.
Hawaiian Electric is to phase in more use of more efficient fossil and renewable generation, the department said.
Including these agreements, the department said the electric utility industry is to deliver 45.5 million metric tons of greenhouse gas reductions in 2000.
